title: Pesticide applicator recertification and supervising noncertified applicators practice questions
description: Practice questions on EPA rules for recertifying pesticide applicators and supervising noncertified applicators (40 CFR 171.107, 171.201).

questions.question: Under 171.107(a), each commercial and private applicator certification expires how long after issuance, unless the applicator is recertified?

options.A: Seven years
options.B: Five years
options.C: Ten years
options.D: Fifteen years

questions.explanation: 171.107(a): "Each commercial and private applicator certification shall expire five years after issuance, unless the applicator is recertified in accordance with this section."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.107, Standards for recertification of certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A State certifying authority wants its applicators to recertify more often than the federal certification period. What does 171.107(a) say about this?

options.A: A certifying authority may establish a shorter certification period.
options.B: Only EPA may set a certification period other than the federal one.
options.C: A certifying authority may shorten the period only for commercial applicators.
options.D: A certifying authority may change the period only if it uses continuing education.

questions.explanation: 171.107(a) states: "A certifying authority may establish a shorter certification period."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.107, Standards for recertification of certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: For a certified applicator's certification to continue without interruption, when must the applicator be recertified under 171.107?

options.A: Within 90 days after the current certification expires
options.B: Within 12 months after the current certification expires
options.C: At the next exam session offered after the certification expires
options.D: Before the expiration of his or her current certification

questions.explanation: 171.107(a): to continue without interruption, "the certified applicator must be recertified under this section before the expiration of his or her current certification."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.107, Standards for recertification of certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An applicator plans to recertify through an online continuing education course. Under 171.107(b)(2)(iii), what must the certifying authority ensure that such a course includes?

options.A: A proctored final exam at a testing center
options.B: A minimum of eight hours of instruction
options.C: A process to verify the applicator's successful completion of the course or event
options.D: A printed certificate mailed to the applicator's employer

questions.explanation: Under 171.107(b)(2)(iii), any continuing education course or event, "including an online or other distance education course or event," relied upon for recertification must include "a process to verify the applicator's successful completion of the course or event."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.107, Standards for recertification of certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: To whom does 171.201 apply?

options.A: Any person who sells restricted use pesticides to noncertified persons
options.B: Any noncertified person who uses general use pesticides at work
options.C: Any certified applicator who allows or relies on a noncertified applicator to use a restricted use pesticide under the certified applicator's direct supervision
options.D: Only commercial applicators who employ noncertified applicators full time

questions.explanation: 171.201(a): "This section applies to any certified applicator who allows or relies on a noncertified applicator to use a restricted use pesticide under the certified applicator's direct supervision."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.201, Requirements for direct supervision of noncertified applicators by certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A certified applicator will supervise a noncertified applicator's use of a restricted use pesticide. Under 171.201(b)(1)(ii), in which categories must the certified applicator be certified?

options.A: In each category applicable to the supervised pesticide use
options.B: In any one category, regardless of the supervised use
options.C: In the category the noncertified applicator's employer holds
options.D: Only in the category that covers the supervisor's own applications

questions.explanation: 171.201(b)(1)(ii): "The certified applicator must be certified in each category as set forth in §§ 171.101 and 171.105(a) through (f) applicable to the supervised pesticide use."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.201, Requirements for direct supervision of noncertified applicators by certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 171.303(a)(7), what may a State certification plan do instead of including standards for direct supervision of noncertified applicators?

options.A: Leave supervision rules to each employer
options.B: Adopt supervision standards below those in 171.201 for private applicators
options.C: Allow noncertified use without supervision standards when the label permits it
options.D: State that use by noncertified applicators is not permitted

questions.explanation: The plan must include supervision standards that "meet or exceed those standards prescribed by the Agency under § 171.201, or must state that use by noncertified applicators is not permitted."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.303, Requirements for State certification plans (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: What each noncertified applicator must meet
questions.question: A 16-year-old will use a restricted use pesticide under the direct supervision of a parent who is a certified private applicator. Which of these is one of the conditions in 171.201(b)(2)(iii) that must be met?

options.A: The application is made only outside school hours
options.B: The restricted use pesticide is not a fumigant, sodium cyanide, or sodium fluoroacetate
options.C: The noncertified applicator holds a State learner's permit
options.D: The application is made aerially only with the parent on board

questions.explanation: The 16-year minimum applies only if all listed requirements are met, including that "The restricted use pesticide is not a fumigant, sodium cyanide, or sodium fluoroacetate."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.201, Requirements for direct supervision of noncertified applicators by certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: What each noncertified applicator must meet
questions.question: What time period does 171.201(b)(2)(ii) set for the noncertified applicator's instruction in the safe operation of the equipment he or she will use?

options.A: Within the last five years
options.B: Within the last three years
options.C: At any time before the first use, with no time limit
options.D: Within the last 12 months

questions.explanation: The noncertified applicator must have "been instructed within the last 12 months in the safe operation of any equipment he or she will use for mixing, loading, transferring, or applying pesticides."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.201, Requirements for direct supervision of noncertified applicators by certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: What each noncertified applicator must meet
questions.question: Which of these is one of the qualifications in 171.201(c) that a noncertified applicator may meet before using a restricted use pesticide under direct supervision?

options.A: Having met the training requirements for an agricultural handler under 40 CFR 170.501 within the last 12 months
options.B: Having worked for the supervising applicator's business for at least six months
options.C: Having read the product label in the presence of the supervisor
options.D: Having watched another worker make the same application

questions.explanation: One listed qualification is: "The noncertified applicator has met the training requirements for an agricultural handler under 40 CFR 170.501 of this title within the last 12 months."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.201, Requirements for direct supervision of noncertified applicators by certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: The labeling of a restricted use pesticide requires personal protective equipment for mixing and loading. Under 171.201(b)(3)(ii), what must the supervising certified applicator ensure for a noncertified applicator doing that work?

options.A: That the noncertified applicator chooses equipment the supervisor considers equivalent to the labeling
options.B: That the noncertified applicator signs a statement accepting the risk
options.C: That the noncertified applicator has clean, labeling-required personal protective equipment in proper operating condition, worn and used correctly for its intended purpose
options.D: That the equipment is inspected by the State once a year

questions.explanation: 171.201(b)(3)(ii): the certified applicator "must ensure that any noncertified applicator has clean, labeling-required personal protective equipment in proper operating condition and that the personal protective equipment is worn and used correctly for its intended purpose."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.201, Requirements for direct supervision of noncertified applicators by certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 171.201(b)(3)(vi), when must the certified applicator be physically present at the site of the use being supervised?

options.A: Only during aerial applications
options.B: When required by the product labeling
options.C: Only when the noncertified applicator is under 18
options.D: Only on the first day of a job that lasts several days

questions.explanation: 171.201(b)(3)(vi): "The certified applicator must be physically present at the site of the use being supervised when required by the product labeling."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.201, Requirements for direct supervision of noncertified applicators by certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 171.201(b)(3)(iv), when must the certified applicator ensure that equipment a noncertified applicator uses for mixing, loading, transferring, or applying pesticides is in proper operating condition as intended by the manufacturer?

options.A: Before each day of use
options.B: Once at the start of each season
options.C: Once a month
options.D: Only when the equipment is first purchased

questions.explanation: 171.201(b)(3)(iv): "The certified applicator must ensure that before each day of use equipment used for mixing, loading, transferring, or applying pesticides is in proper operating condition as intended by the manufacturer".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.201, Requirements for direct supervision of noncertified applicators by certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which of these is one of the criteria in 171.201(d)(2) that the person who conducts noncertified applicator training may meet?

options.A: Having at least two years of field experience as a crew supervisor
options.B: Having completed the noncertified applicator training as a trainee
options.C: Being employed by the registrant of the pesticide product used
options.D: Being currently designated as a trainer of certified applicators or pesticide handlers by EPA, the certifying authority, or a State, Tribal, or Federal agency having jurisdiction

questions.explanation: One listed criterion is to "Be currently designated as a trainer of certified applicators or pesticide handlers by EPA, the certifying authority, or a State, Tribal, or Federal agency having jurisdiction."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.201, Requirements for direct supervision of noncertified applicators by certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Noncertified applicator training is presented audiovisually. What does 171.201(d)(1) require of the person conducting the training?

options.A: To be reachable by phone within 24 hours of the session
options.B: To give each trainee a written test afterward
options.C: To be present during the entire training program and respond to the noncertified applicators' questions
options.D: To send the training video to the certifying authority

questions.explanation: 171.201(d)(1): "The person conducting the training must be present during the entire training program and must respond to the noncertified applicators' questions."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.201, Requirements for direct supervision of noncertified applicators by certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 171.201(e)(3), where, and for how long, must a supervising commercial applicator have access to the records documenting a noncertified applicator's qualifications?

options.A: At the application site, for 12 months from the date of training
options.B: At the commercial applicator's principal place of business, for two years from the date the noncertified applicator used the restricted use pesticide
options.C: At the State lead agency, for five years from the date of certification
options.D: At the commercial applicator's principal place of business, for one year from the date of hire

questions.explanation: 171.201(e)(3): the commercial applicator "must have access to records ... at the commercial applicator's principal place of business for two years from the date the noncertified applicator used the restricted use pesticide."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.201, Requirements for direct supervision of noncertified applicators by certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 171.201(e)(2), when must a commercial applicator create or verify the existence of the record of a noncertified applicator's qualifications?

options.A: Within 30 days after the noncertified applicator first uses the pesticide
options.B: By the end of the application season
options.C: Only when a State inspector asks for it
options.D: Before allowing the noncertified applicator to use restricted use pesticides under his or her direct supervision

questions.explanation: 171.201(e)(2): the commercial applicator must create or verify the record "before allowing the noncertified applicator to use restricted use pesticides under his or her direct supervision."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.201, Requirements for direct supervision of noncertified applicators by certified applicators (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 171.301(a), where is a certification issued under a particular certifying authority's certification plan valid?

options.A: Only within the geographical area specified in the certification plan approved by the Agency
options.B: In every State, Tribe and Federal agency program
options.C: Anywhere in the United States for private applicators only
options.D: Anywhere the applicator's employer does business

questions.explanation: 171.301(a): such a certification "is only valid within the geographical area specified in the certification plan approved by the Agency."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.301, General (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A crew will use a restricted use pesticide in an area of Indian country. Under 171.307, which of these is one of the ways an applicator there may use it?

options.A: Holding a certification from any State, whether or not it is valid in that area of Indian country
options.B: Holding a certification that expired within the last 12 months
options.C: Working under the direct supervision of a certified applicator whose certification is valid in that area of Indian country
options.D: Working under the direct supervision of a certified applicator whose certification is not valid in that area of Indian country

questions.explanation: 171.307: applicators in Indian country "must hold a certification valid in that area of Indian country, or be working under the direct supervision of a certified applicator whose certification is valid in that area of Indian country."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.307, Certification of applicators in Indian country (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 171.311(b)(3), in an area where EPA administers the certification plan, for what uses may a noncertified applicator use a restricted use pesticide under direct supervision?

options.A: For any use, if the label permits it
options.B: Only for uses in categories authorized by the supervising certified applicator's certification
options.C: For any use the noncertified applicator has been trained for
options.D: Only for uses the State lead agency has approved in writing

questions.explanation: 171.311(b)(3): a noncertified applicator may use a restricted use pesticide only under direct supervision "and only for uses in categories authorized by that certified applicator's certification."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 171.311, EPA-administered applicator certification programs (as of Nov 4, 2026)
